page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor utilizing x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 48 MB of Level 3 cache. Memory allocation is configured at 384 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 1933 GB of local solid-state drive temporary storage. Hardware acceleration extensions include AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic enhancements such as AES and SHA-NI, without dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory and database performance. In memory subsystem testing, the server attained high uncached throughput, yielding 260.21 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 127.25 GB/sec in large-block writes. General compute tests reflect balanced multi-threaded throughput, registering a PassMark CPU score of 50651.26 alongside robust cryptographic processing at 43840.97. Database operation benchmarks scored 22997.62, while static web serving throughput reached 48.57 GB/sec. Conversely, the absence of specialized hardware acceleration creates severe bottlenecks for large language models, where 70B parameter text generation drops to 2.33 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of the 8 GB per vCPU memory profile combined with high-capacity local SSD storage. Consolidating large in-memory footprints onto a single 48-vCPU node reduces operational overhead compared to horizontally distributed instances. The primary tradeoff lies in raw per-core frequency and the lack of discrete accelerators, making the node unsuited for parallel deep learning training. The instance is suited for enterprise relational database engines, Redis caching systems, distributed in-memory analytics, and large-scale web application deployments requiring dense memory buffers.
description: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v5 is an enterprise-grade, memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 384 GB of RAM and 1933 GB of local SSD storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the architecture delivers an 8 GB per vCPU ratio along with AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. In benchmark assessments, the system exhibits strong memory bandwidth, achieving 260.21 GB/sec in large-block reads and 127.25 GB/sec in writes, as well as high-tier scores in PassMark database operations and static web serving throughput. Compute benchmarks show stable multi-core capabilities, though heavy deep learning inference is limited by the absence of discrete GPUs. The instance offers resource efficiency for in-memory databases, Redis clusters, transaction processing, and data warehousing.
